title: Hye Vem
description: Shared foundations for browser applications, with packages you can adopt independently.
text:
## Start with the part you need

Hye Vem is a shared application framework. **Vem Data** is its first package: a browser and React runtime for applications that reuse data across screens, coordinate operations, and handle changes in access.

Install Vem Data on its own. You do not need a Vem UI kit, router, or the rest of a framework suite. Your application chooses its components and backend.

| Your next task | Go here |
| --- | --- |
| Decide whether Vem Data fits | [What Vem Data does](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/start/overview) |
| Run something working | [Try the task board in your browser](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/start/quickstart) |
| Build a screen or editor | [Build with Vem](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/build) |
| Connect a backend | [Connect your data](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/connect) |
| Understand a behavior | [Understand Vem](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/understand) |
| Find an API or fix a problem | [Reference and troubleshooting](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/reference) |

The documentation uses one small task board. Try a behavior, then use the code on that guide to build it in your application.

**Status:** the package is being developed in this repository. The docs describe the checked-in implementation; they do not imply that an npm release is available.

title: What Vem Data does
description: Keep related views up to date without coordinating them in every component.
text:
Imagine a task list, a progress summary, and a notes editor. Completing a task should update both the list and the summary. Opening its details should reuse what is already known. A teammate's update should not erase the notes you are typing.

Vem Data manages that shared information. Components describe what they need; one backend integration teaches Vem where the information comes from and what changes mean.

**[Explore the task board →](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/start/quickstart)**

## What you write

For a feature, you write a query, command binding, or edit binding and render the result. You keep control of the components, layout, and validation.

For a new backend, you write its **domain definition**: how to identify resources, translate responses, handle changes, and report operation outcomes. The browser host connects that definition to shared ownership and events. Those are integration tasks, done once for many features.

## When it fits

Vem is useful when features share information, work outlives a screen, or access can change while the application is open. It includes React hooks and an imperative API and can be consumed independently of other Hye Vem packages.

For one isolated request, the integration may be more than you need. Vem does not supply a backend or decide who is authorized; it applies the rules and evidence your integration provides.

## Choose your path

| You want to… | Start with… |
| --- | --- |
| Build a screen or add a button | [Build with Vem](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/build) |
| Connect your backend | [Define a resource](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/connect/resources) |
| Understand why a read happens | [Shared knowledge](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/understand/acquisition) |
| Look up an API or diagnose a problem | [Reference and troubleshooting](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/reference) |

title: Explore the task board
description: Filter a list, finish a task, and keep an edit safe.
text:
You’re planning a weekend with a friend. Use the small app below, then see what Vem did for you. Each part starts with one thing to try.

### Explore the task board

Three short interactions teach filtering, completing a task, and editing notes. Filtering and an overview share known task data. A command previews completion until its response is known. An edit keeps its draft when a teammate changes the saved note. Each lesson runs the real Vem runtime with a simulated in-page service. Source reads are simulated calls, not HTTP. The application has no SharedWorker or browser persistence.

## What you just used

- **A query** asks for the task information a view needs. Filtering reuses what is already known.
- **A command** asks to complete a task. Its **action** keeps track of progress and the result.
- **An edit session** keeps your draft and the saved version it came from together.

These are the [four concepts](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/start/concepts) used throughout Vem. You do not need to manage requests or subscriptions in a feature component.

## The query behind the list

The task list asks for two fields and an optional filter. The component keeps `openOnly` as ordinary React state:


```tsx
const result = useQuery(
	tasks.list({
		select: ["title", "status"],
		where: openOnly ? { status: "open" } : undefined,
	}),
);
```


To build your own feature, continue to [display data](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/build/display), [add an action](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/build/actions), or [build an editor](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/build/editors). Each guide connects a behavior in the app to the code responsible for it.

<details>
<summary>Where the application ends and the integration begins</summary>

### Three responsibilities

1. Describe what the view needs. Render it with public hooks.
2. Define how backend responses, permissions, and operations work.
3. Connect tabs to one owner, with events and optional storage.

The tab holds a read model for synchronous rendering. The SharedWorker owns acquisition and mutation. Pure read definitions run in both places; credentials and HTTP stay in the owner integration.

The examples use Vem’s real runtime with a simulated task service. To connect your application, start with [defining a resource](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/connect/resources). The [browser-host guide](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/connect/browser-host) shows how to share it between tabs.

</details>

- [Access and disclosure](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/understand/access): independent permissions, selective forgetting, and restoration.

title: When Vem reads from the service
description: Reuse known information and acquire only what a view still needs.
text:
Once a task list has loaded, filtering it should feel instant. Opening another view should reuse the same information. Try both in the app below.

### Experiment: Filter without fetching

Choose To do, open the overview, then open the walk’s notes.

Filtering and the overview reuse the task list. Opening notes asks for a missing field, so it reads once more. Returning to that detail reuses the new information.

Runs a deterministic simulated source with the real Vem runtime. Interactive controls are available in the HTML page; no JavaScript is needed to read this explanation.

## A query describes a need

Vem first projects information it already knows and is allowed to show. Vem combines missing requirements across active consumers, including other tabs, and chooses among the backend capabilities declared by the integration. One response may satisfy several views; existing or in-flight information changes what is worth reading.

### From need to knowledge

1. Collect what active consumers across tabs still need.
2. Subtract known facts and account for work already in flight.
3. Choose compatible reads using coverage, permissions, and cost.
4. Publish actual evidence, then plan for any remaining gaps.

The shared owner combines demand from tabs and imperative readers, subtracts known information, and reuses in-flight work. It compares declared backend capabilities and costs. Responses establish facts; missing information may require another source.

## What is actually missing?

| The view needs… | What Vem must know |
| --- | --- |
| A list of tasks | Which tasks belong to the collection |
| Task titles | The selected field on each known task |
| Only unfinished tasks | Each candidate's status, even if status is not displayed |
| A definite empty state | Complete membership and enough information to evaluate the filter |

A missing title leaves a known task visible as an incomplete row. A missing status cannot establish whether a task matches the unfinished filter. [Partial results](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/build/partial-results) shows how to render both.

## A query is not a request cache key

Different queries can reuse the same facts. A list response that includes notes can satisfy a later notes view. If a detail response contains only one task's notes, opening a different task needs another read. The response's actual contents determine what becomes known.

To see Vem choose between competing reads across several views, try [the automatic planning example](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/connect/planning#plan-for-the-whole-application).

The definition declares `sources`: available representations, fields, membership, supported filters, access, and relative cost. Vem plans automatically across the combined demand. [Connect a resource](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/connect/resources) shows the declarations; [how Vem chooses reads](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/connect/planning) explains the selection and its bounds. Feature components only describe information.

## Is this field kept current?

Three questions stay separate: **may I see it**, **what was observed**, and **what keeps that observation current**. Permission answers the first; source responses answer the second; declared event continuity answers the third.

A task's status can be `live` while its notes are a `snapshot` from the last read. An `immutable` field needs no change monitoring because it cannot change for that identity. Vem reports these states per field; an open socket alone does not establish any of them.

Snapshots remain useful without automatic time-based verification. A known gap in the field's declared change coverage makes it stale and can require acquisition. A gap in another field's or project's channel does not. Domain authors [declare that coverage explicitly](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/connect/events#declare-which-fields-the-events-keep-current).

## What makes Vem acquire again?

A new unsatisfied view, retrying unsuccessful acquisition, or a reported event-coverage gap can require new evidence. Mounting, focusing, or waiting a fixed time does not by itself make ordinary data expire.

Events can provide the missing values directly. When an older request finally returns, it cannot overwrite newer established observations or revive values under retired permissions.

<details>
<summary>Measurements that intentionally repeat</summary>

Measurements such as CPU usage are different from ordinary task data. A query can explicitly request a sample interval:


```ts
import { defineResource } from "@hyecompany/vem-data";

export const machines = defineResource<{ usage: number }, { id: string }>()({
	name: "machines",
	fields: ["usage"],
});
export const measuredUsage = machines.get(
	{ id: "web" },
	{
		select: ["usage"],
		sample: { fields: ["usage"], intervalMs: 1000 },
	},
);
```


Import `defineResource` from `@hyecompany/vem-data`. Subscribe with `useQuery(measuredUsage)`. The host also needs a `machines` definition that acquires usage. Sampled fields must be selected; intervals must be finite and at least 100 ms. Sampling ends when consumer demand ends, and does not make unrelated data expire.

</details>

## Why reload might make no request

A reloaded tab can rejoin an owner that still has the needed information. If the owner stopped, a new one can restore eligible data. Permitted values remain displayable, but non-immutable evidence—including plain snapshots—restores stale and the first active need reacquires it. Genuine immutable evidence can survive without another read. This re-establishes evidence after owner loss; it is not a mount, focus, or time-based policy. The integration also establishes the new owner's event continuity. Look at the owner's connection and coverage, not only the page reload, when diagnosing a missing request.

title: Why information disappears after an access change
description: Keep readable information and forget only what lost its permission.
text:
A task's title can be public while its notes are private. You might be able to read those notes because you belong to a team, because you were invited directly, or both. Try removing each permission.

### Experiment: Who can still read the notes?

Turn off Team access, then the direct invitation.

Either permission can disclose the same private note. Losing both removes the note while the public task survives. A reply captured before withdrawal cannot restore that note after regrant; a new authorized update can.

Runs a deterministic simulated source with the real Vem runtime. Interactive controls are available in the HTML page; no JavaScript is needed to read this explanation.

## A value can have more than one permission

Vem keeps the reasons a value may be shown alongside the value. The domain calls these its **disclosure bases**. If either team access or a direct invitation permits the notes, losing just one should not remove them.

| Change | Visible result |
| --- | --- |
| Team access ends; the invitation remains | Notes remain readable |
| The last permission ends | Notes disappear, including from managed edit drafts |
| Write permission ends, but read access remains | The draft stays; saving is disabled |
| Access is granted again | New authorized evidence can restore the notes |

Derived values and relationships also depend on the information and permissions supporting them. A total computed from unreadable records must not remain visible merely because the total was computed earlier.

## Unknown is different from denied

A fresh owner may not yet know who the caller is. Protected restored data stays hidden until the host establishes access. That uncertainty is not proof that permission was revoked.

Likewise, a network error during an established session is not a logout. Only an actual access decision or authority retirement withdraws the old permission. A logout can retire private access while leaving public data and the runtime alive.

## An old reply cannot undo withdrawal

A pending read carries the permission generation under which it started. If that permission is retired, the late response cannot repopulate protected data—even if access was granted again in the meantime. Regrant permits new evidence, not reuse of the retired response.

With persistence, Vem records revocation before deleting saved payloads. Live values disappear immediately even if storage fails; the failure must still be reported because durable cleanup was not established.

To implement these rules, follow [access controls step by step](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/connect/access). Components should render managed query and edit values directly: independent copies in React state or a form library need their own withdrawal integration.

title: What happens when the app closes mid-operation
description: Keep accepted work separate from what the UI knows about it.
text:
An app can close after sending a command but before learning what happened. Sending it again could repeat work. Try returning to an unfinished task below.

### Experiment: Return to an unfinished action

Complete the walk, then close and reopen the example.

The first owner records possible submission and sends once. A replacement owner restores its journal and investigates. Missing confirmation leaves the result unknown; recovery never resubmits the command.

Runs a deterministic simulated source with the real Vem runtime. Interactive controls are available in the HTML page; no JavaScript is needed to read this explanation.

## Sending, watching, and showing are separate

| What happened | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| You navigate away | The shared owner can continue observing the action |
| You dismiss its notice | Feedback is acknowledged; server work is unchanged |
| You lose permission to see it | Protected details disappear; accepted work may continue |
| The owner stops before receiving a result | The next owner needs evidence before deciding what happened |

## Recovery investigates

When storage works, Vem records that submission may occur **before** dispatch. An operation ID returned by the backend can then be saved as recovery metadata. After interruption, the domain's `recover` function uses that metadata to check the backend's operation record.

### Recovery investigates what happened

1. Record possible submission before sending, when storage works.
2. A lost response does not tell us whether the work happened.
3. Restore the action record after access is established.
4. Check what happened. Do not send the command again.

A missing response, missing journal, or missing operation history does not prove that the operation never happened. Recovery is not an instruction to submit again. A lock protects owner exclusivity; a heartbeat timeout cannot transfer ownership.

If the operation record proves success, recovery may report success. If the record is absent or no useful metadata survived, the truthful outcome may be `unknown`. Missing history is not proof that no work occurred. Recovery must not simply call the command again.

The [command implementation guide](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/connect/commands-edits) explains submission and checkpoints. The embedded example intentionally returns an uncertain result so you can see this boundary.

## Storage failure reduces recovery

Actions can still execute if storage fails. Their `recovery` state is then `unavailable`; display that limitation where a user is relying on restart recovery. `RuntimeOptions.onError` receives owner errors such as persistence failures.

## Uploads and background transfers

A command can declare a native HTTP `transfer`. With the [browser transfer host](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/connect/browser-host#let-the-browser-continue-an-upload), the browser can accept responsibility for moving its bytes after tabs close. Without that integration, or when the browser cannot use it, the SharedWorker sends the request while the application remains open.

| Action state | What the UI can say |
| --- | --- |
| `execution.lifetime === "owner"` | Keep an application tab open; show `execution.reason` when present |
| `execution.lifetime === "browser"` | The browser accepted the transfer; closing this tab does not itself cancel it |
| `recovery === "saved"` | The action checkpoint was saved; this alone says nothing about who owns the request |

API support alone does not establish browser ownership. Vem reports `browser` only after an actual handoff acknowledgement or recovered evidence of acceptance. The browser may still stop the transfer, storage may fail, and the server may reject it. The [Background Fetch API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Background_Fetch_API) is not supported by Firefox or Safari; those browsers use the owner lifetime.

The ServiceWorker saves a bounded response receipt in the same protected journal. A returning owner uses that evidence or investigates the existing browser registration; it never starts a replacement upload. If the acknowledgement or result is missing, the outcome can remain `unknown`. A lost acknowledgement does not trigger an owner-bound fallback, because that could send the upload twice.

**Continuation is not resumption.** The journal does not contain the uploaded file, and Vem has no automatic upload replay. A resumable backend needs its own transfer identity and accepted-byte protocol. The [Background Fetch specification](https://wicg.github.io/background-fetch/) restricts automatic request restart to GET because repeating other methods can cause side effects.

The browser uses the request's credential policy; the journal does not pin a cookie, TLS identity, or authenticated session. Credentials can change while work is pending. Server authorization remains authoritative. Read-access loss removes protected activity and receipts; losing write access blocks a handoff that has not started, but does not mean already accepted work was canceled. Explicit cancellation can leave partial remote effects and must not be presented as rollback.

## One owner makes shared decisions

The SharedWorker owns acquisition, actions, and persistence. Tabs own views. A version-independent Web Lock protects ownership, including during updates. A delayed heartbeat does not authorize a second owner.

Use the [browser-host guide](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/connect/browser-host) to configure that boundary. Runtime defaults bound concurrent reads and commands to four each; adjust concurrency and retention through [RuntimeOptions](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/reference/api/runtime.Interface.RuntimeOptions) when your backend or application needs different limits.

title: Troubleshooting
description: Start with what you see, then check the responsible layer.
text:
## Nothing fetched or no event socket

- **In the embedded examples:** the service is simulated inside the page. The counter measures calls to that source, not HTTP requests.
- **In your application:** inspect the existing query's `issues` and whether its requested fields and membership are already known. A satisfied query needs no acquisition.
- **With a SharedWorker host:** inspect the worker's network activity. Page developer tools may not show its requests. Your host opens the event transport; Vem does not choose or open one automatically.

A failed HTTP request is not proof of logout. Check the source URL, proxy, and authentication separately. See [when acquisition happens](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/understand/acquisition).

## Opening another task did not add a service read

The earlier response may have included both tasks' details. Vem reuses all established facts, not only those used by the first view. If it returned only one task, a missing detail on another task should cause acquisition. Check the response contents and your source declarations and response extraction before expecting one request per screen.

## Loading when changing a known filter

Check `readDefinitions` in `connectSharedWorker`: the tab needs the same pure read rules as the owner. Then check the filter fields and `confirmed.complete`. An unknown predicate or incomplete membership can require acquisition.

If the required information is present and permitted, a loading flash is a defect. Do not add a timer or a second feature cache to conceal it. [Browser setup](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/connect/browser-host) shows the shared read definition.

## Partial rows or no confirmed total

A row's `missing` fields, unresolved filter candidates, and incomplete membership mean different things. Keep known rows visible. Only `confirmed.complete` establishes the matching set, and only `result.empty` proves emptiness. [Partial-result rendering](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/build/partial-results) provides the code.

## Save conflict

Confirm that the edit's ETag came from the same response as its baseline. Preserve the draft when the server rejects that token. Let the user reload explicitly; silently replacing the token would turn an old draft into an overwrite of someone else's changes. [Editor recipe](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/build/editors).

## Another tab has different behavior

Start with `client.connectionSnapshot()`. If it is not `ready`, address the reported connection error first. Then compare the tabs' origin, worker URL, and definitions version. Same-origin tabs must use the same ownership lock name across versions. [Host compatibility](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/connect/browser-host#1-agree-on-compatibility).

## A failed action cannot be retried

Default retry requires a settled failure explicitly marked `submitted: false`, and excludes restored actions. A failed response after possible submission does not meet that rule. The domain can override retry only when backend evidence makes another attempt safe. [Command controls](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/build/actions).

## Data disappeared after an access change

Check whether the data lost its last allowed disclosure basis. If it did, disappearance is expected—even from an unsaved draft. Granting permission again allows new evidence; an old response cannot refill the values. [Implementing access](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/connect/access) explains the declarations.

## Recovery is unavailable

Check `action.recovery` and the owner's `onError` reports for persistence failures. Execution can continue while restart recovery is reduced. If a command has no backend operation history to investigate, its journal cannot prove the outcome. [Recovery](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/understand/recovery).

title: Maintainer map
description: Trace a documented behavior to implementation and focused tests.
text:
Paths below are relative to `packages/data`. Read the relevant guide first, then the implementation and behavioral tests. Internal paths are a navigation aid, not import recommendations.

| Behavior | Implementation | Test search |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typed descriptions and selected fields | `src/contracts.ts`, `src/descriptors.ts` | `tests/contracts/`, `tests/types/` |
| Query projection and partial membership | `src/read-model/`, `src/runtime/memberships.ts` | `tests/queries/`, `tests/knowledge/` |
| Missing-information acquisition | `src/runtime/acquisition.ts`, `src/runtime/planning*.ts`, `src/runtime/source-execution.ts`, `src/read-model/requirements.ts` | `tests/planning/` |
| Observations and dependencies | `src/runtime/knowledge.ts`, `src/runtime/relationships.ts` | `tests/knowledge/` |
| Access and restoration | `src/access.ts`, `src/access-proofs.ts`, `src/runtime/restoration.ts` | `tests/access/`, `tests/persistence/` |
| Actions and recovery | `src/actions.ts`, `src/actions/` | `tests/actions/`, `tests/persistence/recovery.test.ts` |
| Managed editing | `src/edit.ts`, `src/runtime/edit-admission.ts` | `tests/editing/` |
| Owner and tab publication | `src/worker.ts`, `src/client.ts`, `src/read-model/` | `tests/host/` |
| Persistence | `src/persistence.ts` | `tests/persistence/` |

The package also keeps liveness and query presentation checks in `tests/queries`, developer-tool checks in `tests/devtools`, and executable-example checks in `tests/examples`. Compile-only assertions in `tests/types/*.types.ts` run through type checking, not the runtime test runner.

At the repository root, `tests/docs` checks the built site, with focused learning tools in `tests/docs/experiments`. `tests/package` checks the actual HTTP/SharedWorker starter, including the packed independent consumer exercised by `scripts/check-package.mjs`. Helpers belong in the nearest `support` directory; only browser launch configuration shared by both suites lives in root `tests/support`.

Before changing a behavior, identify the public contract it affects and add or adjust a focused behavioral test. Keep generic owner and storage mechanics out of domain-specific feature additions.

## Trace a query update

The owner publishes permitted records and membership evidence. A tab applies that publication to its local read model and projects the queries its components use. The owner uses the same projection rules when deciding what information is still missing. Feature code does not manage either copy.

For an existing query, Vem retains each record's contribution: whether it matches, its displayed values, and its missing requirements. A record update recalculates that record's contribution. Unchanged records reuse their previous calculations. Custom scope and filter functions are evaluated again for a changed record; Vem does not assume that these functions read only selected fields.

Before projection, an ordinary observation recalculates currency for changed facts and facts whose evidence depends on them. The dependency index carries changes through derived facts and relationships; it does not treat a new value as evidence that unrelated facts changed. Access changes and event-continuity changes can require broader checks.

This saves repeated evaluation of every resource when one resource changes. Assembling a changed result can still depend on its row count. It is not a constant-time guarantee for every publication.

Access and membership changes can affect which records belong or may be disclosed, so they require broader recomputation. Initial attachment, reset, or a query falling behind the bounded change history can also rebuild its projection. These paths preserve the same results as a full calculation. Inactive retained queries do not perform notification work; reading them again catches up to the current model.

Start with `src/read-model/query-projector.ts` for query contributions, `src/read-model/projection.ts` for the tab's local model, and `src/runtime/read-model-export.ts` plus `src/read-model/publication.ts` for publication changes. Follow the behavior tests in `tests/host` and `tests/queries` before changing their bookkeeping.

## Measure the right work

Run from the repository root:

```sh
node --import tsx scripts/benchmarks/data-publication.mjs 100 1000 5000
node --import tsx scripts/benchmarks/publication-pipeline.mjs 100 1000 5000
```

The first isolates owner observation without active owner queries and tab projection. The second includes active owner queries and three simulated tabs, measuring delta preparation, structured cloning, replica application, and subscriber reads separately. It checks selected-field updates, movement between filters, and updates outside some selections.

These are CPU benchmarks with deterministic data. Their sum is not browser interaction latency: actual Worker scheduling, network, React, and rendering are excluded. Use a browser profile to assess those parts, and behavioral tests to assert which records are evaluated rather than machine-specific timing limits. `packages/data/tests/README.md` documents the benchmark settings and comparison options.

title: Integration limits
description: Know which guarantees your backend and browser host must provide.
text:
## Bound requests that may never return

Vem settles an acquisition when the source answers or fails. The runtime currently has no built-in deadline for a source promise that never settles. This is a gap in the intended finite-read guarantee: a hanging adapter can keep an imperative read pending.

Set transport deadlines in your domain integration. An imperative caller can also bound its own wait:


```ts
import type { DataClient } from "@hyecompany/vem-data";
import { firstTask, tasks } from "../task-board/contract.js";
export function readTaskWithDeadline(client: DataClient) {
	return client.read(tasks.get(firstTask, { select: ["title"] }), {
		signal: AbortSignal.timeout(10_000),
	});
}
```


`DataClient` comes from `@hyecompany/vem-data`; `tasks` is the application's resource contract. Catch an aborted read at the caller. Aborting withdraws that caller's demand, including reads queued before attachment. It does not cancel shared work needed by another view. An acquisition already in flight may finish and contribute permitted evidence; the abandoned reader does not request further acquisition.

## Automatic planning is bounded

Vem chooses acquisition sets from declared capabilities and current knowledge. It cannot infer undocumented backend semantics or know future demand. When record identities or related links are unknown, it may first acquire membership, then plan again with that evidence. Its cost estimates come from the integration; the bounded search keeps the best plan it finds, not a universal optimum.

`maxConcurrent` defaults to 4 source reads. `maxAcquisitionsPerRead` defaults to 4,096 dispatched sources per attempt; exhausting it leaves a partial result with an explanation. Paged sources default to at most 100 pages unless configured. Sources must provide transport deadlines and truthful completeness. These bounds prevent an unbounded acquisition loop; increase them deliberately for larger supported workloads.

## Match promises to your integration

| You want… | Your integration must provide… |
| --- | --- |
| Current data after a disconnected event stream | Accurate field/channel continuity and replay or reacquisition after a gap |
| Private fields to disappear on access loss | Accurate access decisions and disclosure bases |
| Conditional saves | A token from the same writable representation as the draft baseline |
| Recovery after the owner stops | Persistence plus backend evidence the domain can investigate |
| An upload that continues after tabs close | The [browser transfer host](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/connect/browser-host#let-the-browser-continue-an-upload), durable storage, browser support, and confirmed handoff |
| A resumable transfer | A backend transfer protocol and enough durable metadata to resume it |
| Form-library values to be forgotten | Integration that withdraws its values and defaults alongside the edit session |

Vem provides the coordination contracts. It does not generate backend semantics from a schema or supply a form library, authorization server, upload protocol, or development panel.

## What the documentation examples exercise

The embedded examples run Vem against simulated services in the page. They demonstrate shared planning, per-field continuity, actions, access, and edits. Their counters do not represent HTTP traffic; their recovery example uses memory storage.

Repository integration checks separately exercise an actual SharedWorker, HTTP/events, conditional writes, and a packed independent consumer. Backend-specific behaviors still belong in your domain's tests. Use [feature fixtures](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/build/testing) for screens and [the resource guide](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/connect/resources) for integration boundaries.

title: Contribute to these docs
description: Keep guides, examples, reference, and exports in sync.
text:
## Update a guide

Edit `packages/docs/content/handbook`. Lead with the task and prerequisites, show a small useful example, explain the decisions the reader must make, and link a relevant next step. Add a page's title, description, and order in frontmatter. Navigation and machine-readable exports are generated from that content.

Run `npm run docs:prepare` after content changes, then `npm run docs:dev` to preview. Generated content in `content/docs`, `.generated`, and the static `out` artifact is not edited by hand. Source typechecking excludes the previous `out` artifact; the actual example files are compiled separately. During a running preview, rerun `docs:prepare` to publish source changes.

## Show executable code

Put runnable TypeScript in `packages/data/examples`, imported only through public package entries. Mark a focused region with `// #region name` and `// #endregion name`. Use an `Example` include with its file and optional region in a guide. The generator inserts that exact code. Include the code needed for the task on the page; a source link should never be required to understand an omitted step.

Compile examples with `npm run typecheck`. Add negative type assertions for important boundaries such as unselected fields, invalid command inputs, and proposal targets. Do not maintain a second hand-copied tutorial implementation.

## Add a diagram or experiment

Diagram content lives in `content/diagrams.json`. Each node keeps its title, icon, color, and short explanation together. Static diagrams should explain the whole relationship at a glance. Use interaction only when changing something teaches a behavior that a static picture cannot. Add an icon to the small map in `components/Flow.tsx` when needed.

Experiment prompts and explanations live in `content/experiments.json`; focused implementations live in `components/labs`. Start with one useful move the reader can make, then make its result easy to see. Keep technical scope and longer explanations in the expandable section.

The task board at `components/TaskBoardDemo.tsx` is a short, ordered walkthrough of the same lessons used in the guides. `components/lesson` owns the shared application view and teaching presentation, using shadcn components. `components/labs/sources` owns each controlled source. Both use public Vem APIs.

Give each lesson one familiar task first. Explain the observed result in one sentence, after the interaction. Keep unusual responses and permission changes in optional controls. Teach with the app, not a panel of internal state. Match the guide’s technical explanation to that experience, and verify the initial state as well as the failure paths.

Tutorial snippets are extracted from compiled files in `packages/data/examples`. Keep each excerpt focused, and show or explain the imports and local values it needs. The repository fixture separately checks HTTP and SharedWorker integration; running it is a contributor check, not a reader prerequisite. The in-page lessons use simulated calls, so never label their counters as HTTP traffic.

Each experiment needs an initial state, a few labeled controls, reset, observable results, and honest execution scope. Keep interaction user-controlled and keyboard accessible. Add browser checks for reset and meaningful failure paths. Avoid one combined control panel that requires learning every concept at once.

## Change the API reference

Update JSDoc on the public source declaration. `scripts/generate-reference.mjs` reads the package's seven export entry points through pinned TypeDoc and its Markdown plugin. Signatures and member lists are generated; semantic responsibilities belong in source comments and the relevant guide.

## Review the teaching value

Read the rendered page as someone doing the task for the first time. Can they tell where the code belongs, understand its inputs, and use its output without opening a source repository? Explain one practical default before introducing optional mechanisms. Remove repeated scope disclaimers, unexplained API lists, and controls that do not teach anything new.

## Validate the reader journeys

```sh
npm run check
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run test:package
npm run docs:build
npm run test:docs
```

For Pages, build with `BASE_PATH=/vem-web` in the environment. Check search, links and anchors, mobile width, zoom, keyboard focus, reduced motion, and ordinary reading with JavaScript disabled. Do not publish as a side effect of local validation.

`llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`, and `docs.json` come from the same content. Text exports expand code excerpts and explain diagrams and experiments; they must not contain unresolved component tags.

For host development, `npm run example:dev` starts the repository's HTTP/event fixture and SharedWorker application on `http://127.0.0.1:4310`. Use it to investigate transport or cross-tab behavior. The learning examples remain embedded in the docs.
